cards.front: CAM diagnosis requires acute onset + [___] + (disorganised thinking OR altered consciousness).
cards.context: The CAM algorithm requires Feature 1 + Feature 2 + (Feature 3 OR Feature 4) for a positive diagnosis. Feature 2 (inattention) is always required — it's the hallmark of delirium.

cards.front: Vancomycin loading dose: [___] mg/kg IV.
cards.context:
Vancomycin efficacy is AUC/MIC-driven (total-exposure dependent), so a weight-based loading dose front-loads exposure to reach target quickly.

Subsequent dosing is titrated to an AUC of 400-600 (legacy surrogate: trough 15-20 mg/L), balancing efficacy against nephrotoxicity.

cards.front: Preoperative fasting times: [___] hours for solids and 2 hours for clear fluids.
cards.context: Managing medications perioperatively is a key preoperative assessment skill. Some drugs must continue, others must be withheld.

cards.front: Abdominal compartment syndrome: bladder IAP >20 mmHg + new organ dysfunction. Shock type: obstructive (compresses [___]).
cards.context:
Mechanism: rising intra-abdominal pressure compresses IVC → ↓ venous return → obstructive shock (like tamponade or massive PE).

Multi-system failure: oliguria, ↑ airway pressures (splinted diaphragm), gut ischaemia.

Trigger is bladder pressure, not waiting for the textbook tense abdomen.

cards.front: Delta ratio setup: delta anion gap = measured AG minus [___]; delta bicarbonate = 24 minus measured bicarbonate.
cards.context:
Delta ratio = ΔAG ÷ ΔHCO₃⁻. ΔAG = measured AG minus normal AG (12). ΔHCO₃⁻ = normal HCO₃⁻ (24) minus measured HCO₃⁻.

Interpretation: <0.4 = pure normal AG acidosis; 0.4-0.8 = mixed high AG + normal AG acidosis; 0.8-2.0 = pure high AG acidosis; >2.0 = high AG acidosis + concurrent metabolic alkalosis.

cards.front: Target lactate clearance in sepsis is >10% in 2–6 hours. Inadequate clearance warrants reassessing [___] and source control.
cards.context:
Repeat lactate at 2-6 hours after starting resuscitation in sepsis. Target is >10% clearance — failure means tissue perfusion isn't improving despite the bundle interventions.

Non-clearing lactate is a trigger to revisit the basics: are we volume-responsive? (passive leg raise, IVC distensibility) Is source control adequate? (drained abscess, removed line.

cards.front: Vasopressin dose: fixed at [___] units/min. Not titrated due to narrow therapeutic window (risk: gut/digital ischaemia).
cards.context: Unlike catecholamines, vasopressin has a narrow therapeutic window — higher doses cause excessive vasoconstriction (gut ischaemia, digital ischaemia). The fixed dose provides benefit without the toxicity of escalation.

cards.front: Severe chest pain with diaphoresis is ATS Category 2 with a maximum wait of [___] minutes.
cards.context:
Severe chest pain with diaphoresis is treated as suspected ACS until proven otherwise — Category 2 (imminently life-threatening) with a 10-minute target.

Category 2 also covers active severe pain unresponsive to ED analgesia, severe head injury, severe trauma, and altered consciousness from any cause.

cards.front: In acute pancreatitis, CRP >[___] mg/L at 48 hours predicts severe disease and necrosis.
cards.context:
CRP rises in pancreatitis as the inflammatory response peaks at 48-72 h.

Persistent elevation or rising trend prompts CT for necrosis assessment and HDU/ICU referral. Day 1 CRP is *not* useful — wait for the 48-h value.

cards.front: Tidal volume is calculated from ideal body weight at [___] mL/kg, not actual weight.
cards.context:
Lung-protective ventilation uses 6-8 mL/kg of *predicted* (ideal) body weight, calculated from height and sex (Devine formula).

The ARDSNet trial showed 6 mL/kg IBW reduced mortality vs 12 mL/kg in ARDS, and the principle now applies to all ventilated patients.

cards.front: Normal lactate upper limit: below [___]. Levels of 2–4 are mildly elevated; above 4 is severe.
cards.context: Lactate 2–4 is mildly elevated and warrants monitoring; above 4 is severe.

cards.front: Pre-anaesthetic fasting: 2 hours for clear fluids and [___] hours for solids.
cards.context:
GA abolishes protective airway reflexes. Gastric contents can regurgitate, causing pulmonary aspiration leading to chemical pneumonitis, ARDS, or death.

Standard fasting: 6 hours for solids, 2 hours for clear fluids — the '2-and-6 rule.'.

cards.front: Shock is defined as inadequate delivery of oxygen and substrate to tissues — *not* a BP threshold. The bedside markers that betray occult shock with a normal BP are rising [___], oliguria, cool peripheries, and altered mental state.
cards.context:
The question shock answers is whether oxygen and substrate are reaching cells, not whether the cuff reads above 90. BP is one driver of perfusion among several (cardiac output, vascular resistance, microcirculation).

This is why occult shock (normal BP, rising lactate, cool peripheries, oliguria) and permissive hypotension exist as separate concepts.

cards.front: A-a gradient = PAO₂ minus [___]. Age-adjusted upper limit (mmHg) ≈ (age÷4) + 4 mmHg.
cards.context:
A-a gradient quantifies gas exchange efficiency. Normal widens with age.

Elevated A-a = intrinsic lung pathology (V/Q mismatch, shunt, diffusion impairment). Normal A-a with hypoxaemia = hypoventilation (lungs fine).

cards.front: Holliday-Segar sodium requirement for 70 kg: 2500 mL × 3 mmol per 100 mL = [___] mmol/day.
cards.context:
Holliday-Segar maintenance estimates daily Na need at ~3 mmol/100 mL (and K at ~2 mmol/100 mL).

Pure 0.9% saline (154 mmol Na/L) over-shoots adult Na requirements 5-fold — give it for resuscitation, not maintenance.

cards.front: Eclampsia is defined as preeclampsia plus [___].
cards.context: HELLP = haemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, low platelets. Preeclampsia is defined as hypertension after 20 weeks gestation PLUS end-organ involvement. Eclampsia = preeclampsia + seizures.

cards.front: In TBI, target PaCO₂ is 35-40 mmHg. Hyperventilation below PaCO₂ 30 causes cerebral vasoconstriction severe enough to worsen [___].
cards.context: Hyperventilation to PaCO₂ below 30 causes severe cerebral vasoconstriction — this can worsen ischaemia in already-injured brain tissue.

cards.front: Inotrope increases myocardial [___], vasopressor causes vasoconstriction, and chronotrope changes heart rate.
cards.context: Use IVC to decode cardiovascular drug actions quickly under pressure.

cards.front: TXA must be given within 3 hours of injury — late administration may [___] mortality (per CRASH-2).
cards.context: CRASH-2 time-to-treatment analyses showed that TXA given after 3 hours appeared to INCREASE death due to bleeding. This is a high-yield exam trap.

cards.front: First-line treatment for torsades de pointes is IV [___] at a dose of 2 g.
cards.context:
Torsades de pointes is polymorphic VT in the setting of QT prolongation — the QRS complexes 'twist' around the isoelectric baseline, alternating positive and negative deflections.

Also: stop QT-prolonging drugs (macrolides, antipsychotics, methadone, ondansetron, hydroxychloroquine), correct K⁺ to >4.5, correct Mg²⁺ to >1.0, isoprenaline or pacing to overdrive >100/min if recurrent.

cards.front: Adding ibuprofen to opioids (multimodal analgesia) reduces opioid requirements by approximately 20–40%. The recommended dose is [___] mg TDS; higher doses increase side effects without proportional benefit.
cards.context:
NSAIDs are opioid-sparing because they block peripheral COX, cutting prostaglandin-driven nociceptor sensitisation at the injury site — a different mechanism to opioids, so the effects stack.

Avoid the add-on in renal impairment, hypovolaemia, active GI bleed/ulcer risk, and after CABG (increased cardiovascular events).

cards.front: Wake-up strokes with unknown onset may qualify for thrombectomy up to [___] hours if CT perfusion imaging shows mismatch.
cards.context:
DAWN (NEJM 2018) and DEFUSE-3 (NEJM 2018) extended the thrombectomy window to 24 hours from last-known-well in patients with proximal large-vessel occlusion AND a favourable imagin.

This transformed wake-up strokes from 'too late' to potentially treatable.

cards.front: Modified-release (MR) paracetamol has [___] absorption. A single level can miss peaks — take 2 levels 4 hours apart.
cards.context: MR formulations like Panadol Osteo have delayed and prolonged absorption. A single nomogram plot can miss ongoing absorption — two levels 4h apart detect the characteristic double peak.

cards.front: In empiric sepsis, if MRSA risk factors are present, add [___].
cards.context: MRSA risk factors include recent hospitalisation, nursing home residence, known MRSA colonisation, or IV drug use. Vancomycin loading dose is 25-30 mg/kg.

cards.front: Ideal ETT position on CXR: [___] cm above the carina (T3-T4 level). Most common malposition is right mainstem intubation.
cards.context:
Right mainstem intubation is the most common ETT malposition because the right main bronchus diverges at a smaller angle from the trachea (25° vs 45° for the left).

Head flexion advances the ETT ~2 cm; extension withdraws it ~2 cm.

cards.front: Adequate sepsis resuscitation targets lactate clearance of ≥10-20% within [___] hours.
cards.context: Lactate clearance indicates improving tissue perfusion — your resuscitation is working. Persistent or rising lactate despite fluids and vasopressors signals inadequate source control or refractory shock.

cards.front: If CT is negative in suspected SAH, the next investigation is [___] performed at least 12 hours from onset.
cards.context:
A thunderclap headache (peak intensity within seconds) carries ~10% probability of SAH. CT sensitivity is ~95% within 6 hours but drops sharply with time as blood breaks down.

Xanthochromia distinguishes true SAH from traumatic tap definitively. Some centres now use CTA instead of LP, but LP at 12 h remains the standard pathway in most Australian EDs.
